abstract: Flotillins organize membrane microdomains implicated in signaling, cell-wall synthesis, and antibiotic resistance, yet how bacterial flotillins assemble remains unknown. Here, we report a 3.1 [A] cryo-EM structure of the Escherichia coli flotillin YqiK, purified through its NfeD-family partner YqiJ - the first high-resolution structure of a bacterial flotillin assembly. YqiK forms a membrane assembly of 54 identical subunits. Unlike human flotillin cages, which contain two alternating paralogues, YqiK assembles from a single transmembrane protein. The cage is ~38 nm wide and encloses ~900 nm2 of membrane within its ring of 54 transmembrane helices. Its wall helices run continuously for ~287 &Aring, the longest in any SPFH assembly, making this the largest membrane-anchored SPFH cage reported to date. In YqiK, helix length and tilt set cage dimensions, while intersubunit salt bridges and hydrophobic interactions stabilize the assembly. Focused classification revealed local discontinuities in the cage wall, suggesting possible conformational flexibility. Mass spectrometry identified stress-associated membrane proteins and respiratory complexes that co-purify with YqiK-YqiJ. Together, these findings reveal how a bacterial flotillin builds a large membrane-associated scaffold and provide a structural basis for investigating how such compartments organize membrane proteins within the microdomain they define.

summary: Cryo-EM structure at 3.1 Å of E. coli flotillin YqiK with partner YqiJ reveals a 54-subunit membrane cage with unusually long wall helices.
title: Structural basis of cage assembly by a bacterial flotillin
